questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions. If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass.

questions.question: What affects the space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If another driver might hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Speed up.
Go the same speed.
Slow down to give them space in front of your vehicle.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver behind you wants to pass. This creates space in front of your car so they can pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: When should you use turn signals when parking next to a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when moving toward the curb to park and when leaving the curb.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Can you park in the handicap parking access aisle next to a handicap parking space?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing.
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should make sure that:

options.text: Only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
All passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the engine, make sure you and all passengers buckle your seat belts.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with sirens or flashing lights approaches?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if you can.
Speed up to keep your right-of-way.
Always stay in your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when it is safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic flow, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic flow, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and blend smoothly with fast-moving traffic. Do not stop like you would on other roads.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Hold the steering wheel tight and use light braking.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and use light braking.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight to keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and braking lightly. Pull off the road safely when possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that you are approaching a railroad crossing.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights or gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Must yield only to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter. Be ready to stop if needed, but you can go if there are no other vehicles nearby.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because your car takes a long distance to stop completely.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Watch far ahead for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging from on-ramps and expect fast changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes are going in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes with traffic going in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the pavement.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use your low beam headlights in fog. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that their vehicle left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that their vehicle left the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's instructions. They override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a citation.
questions.explanation: You must always carry proof of insurance. Show it to an officer after a traffic stop or collision if asked.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the accelerator and slow down gradually. Use light braking only after the vehicle has slowed considerably.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these choices
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal over-the-counter or prescription medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: On a four-lane highway, do you need to stop for a stopped school bus when traveling in the opposite direction?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You do not need to stop when meeting a school bus on a four-lane highway if you are traveling in the opposite direction. However, always be cautious around children.

questions.question: When a bicyclist makes a left turn, what can they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see them use the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: When a child on a bicycle is near your vehicle, what should you expect?

options.text: Beep your horn.
The child to be in total control of the bicycle.
The unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: The unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and may suddenly change direction. Children and bicycles are small and can be hard to see.
